content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapter 25. Supplemental: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 viewpoint concepts. This unit focuses on assets, threats, and controls.

Security analysis starts with assets and threats. Assets are things worth protecting, such as data, credentials, services, availability, reputation, or business operations. Threats describe possible harm to those assets.

Controls are architectural and operational mechanisms that reduce risk. They include identity, authorization, encryption, validation, network segmentation, monitoring, audit, least privilege, and secure defaults.
Studio: for a document-sharing app, identify five assets, three threats, and three architectural controls.

concepts.name: Security asset
concepts.description: A data item, capability, service, credential, or business function that requires protection.

concepts.name: Threat
concepts.description: A potential cause of harm to a security asset or security property.

concepts.name: Security control
concepts.description: A mechanism or process that reduces the likelihood or impact of a security threat.

concepts.name: Least privilege
concepts.description: The design principle that actors and components receive only the permissions required for their responsibilities.
